title: Podoba mi się · smakuje mi · boli mnie
title_en: I like it · it tastes good · it hurts
note: THREE fixed blocks only: podoba mi się, smakuje mi, boli mnie. daj mi DROPPED — the imperative is a whole new system and it does not show the subject-flip, which is the entire reason this unit exists. NOT the dative case: no ci/mu/jej/nam, no noun datives (mamie, bratu), no paradigm table, and the case is never named anywhere in learner text. mi and mnie are taught as words that live inside their block, nothing more. mnie in boli mnie is accusative, not dative — deliberately NOT explained; Dad is told only that boli keeps mnie and podoba/smakuje keep mi. THE POINT: the English subject flips. The film pleases, the coffee tastes, the head hurts; Dad is the person it happens to. Intro slide 2 is built entirely around that, and quiz item 6 (ta kawa, not kawę) makes him act on it. FENCED: no past of any block (podobał mi się) — later; no plural subjects (podobają mi się, bolą mnie nogi) so only the 3sg form of each verb is ever needed; no questions, because czy podoba ci się would need ci. Negation IS included (nie in front of the whole block) — it is already taught, adds no new form, and 'I don't like this' is too high-frequency to withhold. się is treated exactly as a2_sie framed it: a word belonging to the verb, never 'self'. Hook: chce mi się pić is already in the pool, so Dad has been saying mi since A1.

intro.title: One little word you already say
intro.body:
You already have a sentence with mi inside it: chce mi się pić — "I'm thirsty". Nobody has ever told you what that mi is doing there.

mi means "to me" or "for me". mnie is its partner and means "me". Neither of them is ever the one doing the verb. They are the person something happens TO.

Three everyday Polish sentences are built on that idea. Learn each one as a block of words that never comes apart.
intro.body_pl: mi i mnie to nie wykonawca czynności — to osoba, której coś się przydarza.

intro.title: Polish turns the sentence round
intro.body:
This is the one thing to understand in this unit, and it is worth two minutes.

In English you are the one who likes. In Polish you are not. The film does the pleasing. The coffee does the tasting. The head does the hurting. You are simply the person it happens to.

So the thing goes where the doer goes, and it keeps its plain dictionary form — ten film, ta kawa, głowa. It never changes shape. Compare chcę kawę, where the coffee is what you want and takes -ę. Here the coffee is not what you want; it is the one doing the work, so it stays kawa.

Say it to yourself the long way round for the first few days — the film pleases me, the coffee tastes to me, the head hurts me — and the Polish will stop looking strange.
intro.body_pl: To rzecz jest wykonawcą: ten film, ta kawa, głowa. Ja jestem tylko mi albo mnie.

headers: Who does the verb in Polish
rows: ten film — the film does the pleasing
ta kawa — the coffee does the tasting
głowa — the head does the hurting

intro.title: The three blocks, and what follows them
intro.body:
The words inside a block never move. podoba mi się is always those three words in that order, and the się in it is the same się you met in czuję się — it belongs to the verb and is not translated.

No new endings here either. Each verb runs on a present pattern you already own: podoba like mieszka, smakuje like pracuje, boli like mówi. You only ever need this one form, because the doer is always a thing.

After the block comes the thing itself, with ten for masculine, ta for feminine, to for neuter.
intro.body_pl: Blok się nie zmienia. Po bloku: ten, ta albo to + rzecz.

intro.title: boli mnie, and how to say no
intro.body:
boli mnie is a little different in two ways, both of them easy.

First, body parts follow it straight away with no ten, ta or to: Boli mnie głowa. Boli mnie ząb.

Second, you never need a word for "my". Boli mnie already says the head is yours, so Moja głowa boli mnie is wrong — Poles do not say it.

To say you do not like something, put nie in front of the whole block and change nothing inside it. Words like często, czasami, dzisiaj and bardzo go in front of the block too.
intro.body_pl: Boli mnie głowa — bez moja. Przeczenie: nie przed całym blokiem.

quiz.explain: podoba mi się is a fixed block of three words. mnie lives in the other block, boli mnie — each block keeps its own word, and there is nothing to work out.
boli takes mnie, podoba and smakuje take mi. Learn each block with the word that sits inside it and you will never have to choose.
książka is feminine, so ta. The block keeps its mi and keeps its się — drop either one and the sentence breaks.
You say chcę kawę with -ę because there the coffee is what you want. Here the coffee is the one doing the work — it is the thing that tastes — so it stays in its plain form, kawa.
The się was dropped. It belongs to this verb, exactly as it does in czuję się, and its place in the block is after mi.
No word for "my" is needed — boli mnie already says the leg is yours. And noga is the one doing the hurting, so it is singular and in its plain form.
